'''John Corrigan''' "'''Jonathan'''" '''Wells''' (September 19, 1942 – September 19, 2024) was an American [[molecular biologist]], [[cell biologist]], and theologian. He was an advocate of [[intelligent design]], a [[pseudoscientific]] argument for the existence of God.

Wells joined the [[Unification Church of the United States]] in 1974. He earned a doctorate in [[religious studies]] from [[Yale University]] in 1986 and a second doctorate in [[Molecular biology|molecular]] and [[Cell biology|cellular biology]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1994. He subsequently wrote that the teachings of [[Sun Myung Moon]] and his studies at [[Unification Theological Seminary]] convinced him to devote himself to "destroying [[Darwinism]]".<ref name="Forrest">{{cite web |url=http://www.designinference.com/documents/2007.12.MPC_Rise_and_Fall.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080106063508/http://www.designinference.com/documents/2007.12.MPC_Rise_and_Fall.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=2008-01-06 |title=The Rise and Fall of Baylor University's Michael Polanyi Center (Barbara Forrest's Letter to Simon Blackburn) |last=Forrest |first=Barbara |author-link=Barbara Forrest |date=March 2000 |editor-last=Dembski |editor-first=William A |editor-link=William A. Dembski |website=DesignInference.com |publisher=William Dembski |access-date=2013-12-12 |quote=As I stated earlier, Johnson, Dembski, and their associates have assumed the task of destroying 'Darwinism,' 'evolutionary naturalism,' 'scientific materialism,' 'methodological naturalism,' 'philosophical naturalism,' and other 'isms' they use as synonyms for evolution. }} Quoted in [https://web.archive.org/web/20051026133901/http://www.designinference.com/documents/2005.09.Expert_Rebuttal_Dembski.pdf "Rebuttal to Reports by Opposing Expert Witnesses"] (PDF) by William A. Dembski (May 14, 2005).</ref> He became a member of several scientific associations and published in academic journals.

In his book ''[[Icons of Evolution|Icons of Evolution: Science or Myth?]]'' (2000), Wells argued that a number of examples used to illustrate biology textbooks were erroneous or exaggerated. Wells said that this shows that evolution conflicts with the evidence, and so argued against its teaching in [[Creation and evolution in public education|public education]].<ref name="Icons intro" /><ref name="Coyne">{{cite journal |last=Coyne |first=Jerry |author-link=Jerry Coyne |date=April 12, 2001 |title=Creationism by stealth |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |type=Book review |volume=410 |issue=6830 |pages=745–46 |doi=10.1038/35071144 |bibcode=2001Natur.410..745C |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.discovery.org/a/1180 |title=Critics Rave Over ''Icons of Evolution'': A Response to Published Reviews |last=Wells |first=Jonathan |date=June 12, 2002 |website=[[Center for Science and Culture]] |publisher=Discovery Institute |location=Seattle, WA |quote=Several of them grossly exaggerate or distort the truth, while others are patently false. Yet they are found year after year in almost all textbooks dealing with evolutionary theory, and they invariably accompany other material promoting that theory. When someone points out that the textbook examples misrepresent the facts, Darwinists don't rush to correct them. Instead, they rush to defend them. |access-date=2007-08-13}}</ref> Some reviewers of ''Icons of Evolution'' have said that Wells [[Fallacy of quoting out of context|misquoted experts]] cited as sources and took minor issues out of context, basing his argument on a flawed [[syllogism]].<ref name="Coyne" /><ref name="CTH98" /> Wells's views on evolution had been rejected by the [[scientific community]].<ref name="Forrest" /><ref name="Icons intro">{{cite web |url=http://www.iconsofevolution.org/intro/ |title=INTRODUCTION to ICONS of EVOLUTION: Science or Myth? Why much of what we teach about evolution is wrong |last=Wells |first=Jonathan |website=Icons of Evolution |publisher=[[Discovery Institute]] |location=Seattle, WA |access-date=2013-12-12 |quote=Biological evolution is the theory that all living things are modified descendants of a common ancestor that lived in the distant past. It claims that you and I are descendants of ape-like ancestors, and that they in turn came from still more primitive animals.<br>[...]<br>...much of what we teach about evolution is wrong. This fact raises troubling questions about the status of Darwinian evolution. If the icons of evolution are supposed to be our best evidence for Darwin's theory, and all of them are false or misleading, what does that tell us about the theory? Is it science, or myth? |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131229192456/http://www.iconsofevolution.org/intro/ |archive-date=2013-12-29 }}</ref><ref name="wells_PIGDID">{{cite web |url=http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2006/08/the_politically_1.html |title=The Politically Incorrect Guide to Darwinism and Intelligent Design Review: Why Should Words Have Meanings? (Chapter 1) |last=Humburg |first=Burt |editor-last=Cartwright |editor-first=Reed A. |date=August 26, 2006 |website=[[The Panda's Thumb (blog)|The Panda's Thumb]] |publisher=The TalkOrigins Foundation, Inc. |location=Houston, TX |type=Blog |access-date=2007-02-04 |quote=In order to advance his thesis, Wells has to convey the idea that 'Darwinism' pits itself against traditional Christianity: to allow pupils to learn it is to give them up to atheism, decadence, liberalism and to lose the culture war.<br>Note that Wells does not wage war against evolution. In fact, he is at pains to make it (somewhat) clear that he wages war against 'Darwinism', which in context might sound like the sort of thing any sensible Christian would want to guard against. Unfortunately, Wells isn't exactly clear what he means by Darwinism as opposed to evolution.<br>[...]<br>Easily, one of the prominent faults of Wells's screed is a pervasive confusion between terms. Words, like 'Darwinism' and 'Traditional Christianity', seem to mean whatever Wells wants them to mean for that specific sentence. In many cases words are used without regard for his own stated definitions and usually without regard to usage elsewhere in his book. There are several possible reasons for this confusion in terms. First, Wells confusion may be by design. I have argued elsewhere that creationists intend to confuse their audiences when they argue. Second, if you review the acknowledgements page, you'll read how Wells used many authors to help him prepare this text. It is possible that Wells's editorship was so insufficient that he allowed a term that makes up part of the book's very title to have a flexible meaning. My suspicion is that there was both disparity between the understanding of key terms by different authors ''as well as'' an intention to confuse. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061126045754/http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2006/08/the_politically_1.html |archive-date=November 26, 2006 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Wells was born on September 19, 1942, in New York City.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-09-27 |title=Remembering Jonathan Wells |url=https://scienceandculture.com/2024/09/remembering-jonathan-wells-a-key-figure-in-the-intelligent-design-movement/ |access-date=2026-01-22 |website=[[Science and Culture Today]] |language=en-US|last=Dembski|first=William A.|author-link=William A. Dembski}}</ref>{{Sfn|Cashill|2005|p=173}} He was the third child in a family of five children,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2024 |title=Obituary: Jonathan Wells |url=https://obituaries.washtimesherald.com/obituary/jonathan-wells-1091776141 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=[[Washington Times Herald]] |language=en}}</ref> and grew up in northern [[New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klinghoffer |first=David |date=2017-04-18 |title=Jonathan Wells and Zombie Science, Out Today, Could Not Be Timelier |url=https://scienceandculture.com/2017/04/jonathan-wells-and-zombie-science-out-today-could-not-be-timelier/ |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=[[Science and Culture Today]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He was raised [[Presbyterian]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Jonathan |date=November 5, 2011 |title=Here's Jonathan Wells on destroying Darwinism – and responding to attacks on his character and motives |url=https://uncommondescent.com/intelligent-design/heres-jonathan-wells-on-destroying-darwinism-and-responding-to-attacks-on-his-character-and-motives/ |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=Uncommon Descent |via=''[[Science and Culture Today]]''}}</ref> In 1960, Wells graduated from [[Montclair High School (New Jersey)|Montclair High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andre |first=Linda Linnard |title=Jonathan (John) Wells (Deceased), Montclair, NJ New Jersey last lived in Poulsbo, WA USA |url=https://www.montclair60.com/class_profile.cfm?member_id=2372397 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260103014500/https://www.montclair60.com/class_profile.cfm?member_id=2372397 |archive-date=2026-01-03 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=montclair60.com}}</ref>  After high school, he received a full scholarship to attend [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Darwin's Nemesis: Phillip Johnson and the Intelligent Design Movement|url=|publisher=InterVarsity Press|date=2006-02-22|isbn=978-0-8308-2836-4|language=en|first=William A.|last=Dembski|page=85}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> As an undergraduate at Princeton, Wells majored in [[geology]], but dropped out of the university in his junior year.{{Sfn|Cashill|2005|p=173}}

After attending the 1963 [[March on Washington]], Wells became a [[pacifist]] and worked as a taxi driver in New York City. He was drafted into the [[U.S. Army]] and served two years of military service in Germany.{{Sfn|Cashill|2005|p=173}} After being discharged from the army in 1966, he enrolled at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he led a protest against the [[Vietnam War draft]] at [[Sproul Plaza]]. He was arrested for [[draft dodging]] and incarcerated in [[solitary confinement]] for four months, then imprisoned for eight months at the [[United States Disciplinary Barracks|U.S. Disciplinary Barracks]] in [[Fort Leavenworth]].{{Sfn|Cashill|2005|p=173}}

Upon his release from prison, Wells re-enrolled at Berkeley and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in geology and physics with a minor in biology in 1970.{{Sfn|Cashill|2005|p=173}}<ref>[https://www.tparents.org/Library/Unification/Talks/Wells/Wells-150902.pdf Jonathan Wells Recalls His Days at UTS] </ref> He recalled that, as an undergraduate, "I became an agnostic and a Darwinist".<ref name=":2" /> After graduation, he lived in rural [[Mendocino County]], where "I ceased being an agnostic and a Darwinist".<ref name=":2" /> He joined the [[Unification Church of the United States]] in 1974, then began attending the [[Unification Theological Seminary]] in 1976.<ref name=":2" /> While studying at [[Columbia University]], he recalled that he "became convinced that the Darwinian mechanism of accidental mutations and natural selection is incapable of producing the changes required by evolution".<ref name=":2" />

Wells graduated from seminary in 1978 and was awarded a scholarship to pursue doctoral studies at [[Yale University]].<ref name=":2" /> He earned a [[Master of Arts]]<ref name=":0" /> from Yale in 1980 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[religious studies]] from Yale in 1986.<ref name="Numbers381">[[#Numbers 2006|Numbers 2006]], p. 381</ref> His doctoral dissertation at Yale, completed under theologian [[David Kelsey]], was titled, "Charles Hodge's critique of Darwinism: The argument to design".<ref>{{Cite web |date=1986 |title=Charles Hodge's critique of Darwinism: The argument to design |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/027a4d44921641ea88fef1fb21130632/1?cbl=18750&diss=y&pq-origsite=gscholar |access-date=22 January 2025 |publisher=[[Proquest]] |type=PhD Thesis}}</ref>

In 1994, Wells earned a second doctorate, a Ph.D. in [[molecular biology]] and [[cellular biology]], from the [[University of California, Berkeley]].{{Sfn|Numbers|2006|p=381}} His doctoral dissertation at Berkeley was titled, "A confocal microscopy study of microtubule arrays involved in cortical rotation during the first cell cycle of Xenopus embryos".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=1994 |title=A confocal microscopy study of microtubule arrays involved in cortical rotation during the first cell cycle of Xenopus embryos |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/ecf55df85535289a2fab8436336562b1/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=18750&diss=y |access-date=22 January 2025 |publisher=[[Proquest]] |type=PhD Thesis}}</ref> Among his doctoral advisors at Berkeley was the herpetologist [[David B. Wake]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
After receiving his second doctorate, Wells supervised a hospital laboratory in [[Fairfield, California]], from 1994 to 1998.<ref name="Wells autobiography" /> Concurrently, he was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in molecular and cellular biology at Berkeley from 1995 to 1998,<ref name="Wells autobiography">{{cite web |url=http://www.darwinismandid.com/then/index.php |title=Jonathan Wells (1942-2024) |last= |first= |website=darwinismandid.com |publisher=[[Discovery Institute]] |location=Seattle, WA |access-date=2008-07-16|date=2005}}</ref> during which time he wrote articles critical of Darwinism.<ref name="2phd">{{cite web |url=http://www.tparents.org/library/unification/talks/wells/DARWIN.htm |title=Darwinism: Why I Went for a Second Ph.D. |last=Wells |first=Jonathan |website=True Parents Organization |location=Denver, CO |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref> 

In 1996, Wells started working for the [[Center for Science and Culture]] (then the Center for the Renewal of Science and Culture) at the Discovery Institute, a conservative evangelical think tank, where he was appointed the Karl Ernst von Baer Fellow in Developmental and Evolutionary Biology.{{Sfn|Numbers|2006|p=382–383}}<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.discovery.org/p/41 |title=Jonathan Wells, Senior Fellow - CSC |website=Discovery Institute |location=Seattle, WA |access-date=2013-12-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314204248/http://www.discovery.org/p/41 |archive-date=2013-03-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He served as one of the associate editors of the ''[[Origins & Design]]'' intelligent design journal, along with [[William A. Dembski]] and [[Stephen C. Meyer]].{{Sfn|Numbers|2006|p=383}} He also worked at the [[International Society for Complexity, Information, and Design]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iscid.org/fellows.php |title=Society Fellows |website=International Society for Complexity, Information, and Design |location=Princeton, NJ |access-date=2013-12-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116054926/http://www.iscid.org/fellows.php |archive-date=2013-01-16 }}</ref> which also promoted intelligent design.<ref name="aaas">{{cite web |url=http://www.aaas.org/spp/dser/03_Areas/evolution/issues/peerreview.shtml |title=Intelligent Design and Peer Review |website=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] |location=Washington, D.C. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312080527/http://www.aaas.org/spp/dser/03_Areas/evolution/issues/peerreview.shtml |archive-date=2007-03-12 |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref>

Wells had written on the subject of marriage within the Unification Church, and had been called a "Unification Church marriage expert" by church sources.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tparents.org/library/unification/talks/wells/MARRGE3.htm |title=Marriage and the Family: the Unification Blessing |last=Wells |first=Jonathan |website=True Parents Organization |location=Denver, CO |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Lanham |first=Cheryl Wetzstein |date=September 1994 |title=True Subject and Object, Not Men and Women |url=http://www.tparents.org/UNews/Unws9409/QUINN-01.htm |work=Unification News |type=Letter to the editor (reprint) |location=New York |publisher=[[Unification Church|Holy Spirit Association for the Unification of World Christianity]] |issn=1061-0871 |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tparents.org/Library/Unification/Photos/Uph-1997/0-Toc.htm |title=Unificationist Photos from 1997 and 1998 |website=True Parents Organization |location=Denver, CO |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref> Wells defended Unification Church theology against what he said were unfair criticisms of it made in 1977 by the [[National Council of Churches]].<ref name="Antal">{{cite web |url=http://www.tparents.org/Library/Unification/Talks/Antal/Antal_nccc.htm |title=New Hope for Dialogue with National Council of Churches of Christ |last=Antal |first=Chris |date=February 2000 |website=True Parents Organization |location=Denver, CO |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref>

Wells appeared on a panel at [[Harvard]] with [[Stephen Palumbi]] in November 2001, which his supporters lauded as a "[[home run]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://arn.org/docs/pjweekly/pj_weekly_011202.htm|title=The Weekly Edge Update: Wells Hits a Home Run at Harvard|date=2001-12-02|first=Phillip E.|last=Johnson|website=[[Access Research Network]]|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/2001/11/29/panelists-discuss-validity-of-evolutionary-theory/|title=Panelists Discuss Validity Of Evolutionary Theory|date=2001-11-29|first=Jeslyn A.|last=Miller|work=The Harvard Crimson|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://old.richarddawkins.net/articles/119-why-i-won-39-t-debate-creationists|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130312033731/http://old.richarddawkins.net/articles/119-why-i-won-39-t-debate-creationists|archive-date=2013-03-12|url-status=dead|title=Why I Won't Debate Creationists|date=2006-05-14|first=Richard|last=Dawkins|website=The Richard Dawkins Foundation for Reason and Science|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrwzYOBLUoE |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/NrwzYOBLUoE |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Evolution vs Creation debate—Harvard Professor Stephen Palumbi vs Jonathan Wells|date=2013-11-17|website=Youtube|access-date=2018-10-03}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Other observers stated that Wells' performance was "uneventful".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/2003/3/31/death-to-intelligent-design-just-months/|title=Death to Intelligent Design|date=2003-03-31|first=Jonathan H.|last=Esensten|work=The Harvard Crimson|access-date=2018-10-03}}</ref>

==Opposition to Darwinian evolution==
{{Intelligent Design}}

Of his student days at Unification Theological Seminary (1976–78), Wells said, "One of the things that Father [Reverend Sun Myung Moon] advised us to do at UTS was to pray to seek God's plan for our lives." Wells later described that plan: "To defend and articulate Unification theology especially in relation to Darwinian evolution."<ref>{{cite journal |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=May–June 1997 |title=Dr. Jonathan Wells Returns to UTS |url=http://www.tparents.org/library/unification/publications/cornerst/cs970506/CST_Dr-Jonathan.html |journal=The Cornerstone |issn=0197-5196 |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref>

Wells stated that his religious doctoral studies at Yale, which were paid for by the Unification Church, focused on the "root of the conflict between Darwinian evolution and Christian doctrine" and encompassed the whole of Christian [[theology]] within a focus of Darwinian controversies.<ref name="2phd" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dailykos.com/story/2006/01/15/178574/-Know-Your-Creationists |title=Know Your Creationists |last=Andrew |first=Stephen |date=January 15, 2006 |website=[[Daily Kos]] |publisher=Kos Media, LLC |location=Berkeley, CA |type=Blog |oclc=59226519 |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref> He said:
{{blockquote|...I learned (to my surprise) that biblical chronology played almost no role in the 19th- century controversies, since most theologians had already accepted geological evidence for the age of the earth and re-interpreted the days in [[Book of Genesis|Genesis]] as long periods of time. Instead, the central issue was design.<ref name="2phd" />}}

Wells said that "destroying Darwinism" was his motive for studying Christian theology at Yale and going on to seek his second PhD at Berkeley, studying biology and in particular [[embryology]]:
{{blockquote|Father's <nowiki>[Rev. Moon's]</nowiki> words, my studies, and my prayers convinced me that I should devote my life to destroying Darwinism, just as many of my fellow Unificationists had already devoted their lives to destroying [[Marxism]]. When Father chose me (along with about a dozen other seminary graduates) to enter a Ph.D. program in 1978, I welcomed the opportunity to prepare myself for battle.<ref name="2phd" />}}

Wells's statement and others like it are viewed by the scientific community as evidence that Wells lacks proper scientific [[Objectivity (science)|objectivity]] and mischaracterizes evolution by ignoring and misrepresenting the evidence supporting it while pursuing an agenda promoting notions supporting his religious beliefs in its place.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2004/03/mything_the_poi.html |title=Mything the point: Jonathan Wells' bad faith |date=March 30, 2004 |last=Wilkins |first=John S. |website=The Panda's Thumb |publisher=The TalkOrigins Foundation, Inc. |location=Houston, TX |type=Blog |access-date=2014-01-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924063710/http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2004/03/mything_the_poi.html |archive-date=September 24, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/01/jonathan_wells_knows_nothing_a.php |title=Jonathan Wells knows nothing about development, part I |last=Myers |first=PZ |author-link=PZ Myers |date=January 24, 2007 |website=[[Pharyngula (blog)|Pharyngula]] |publisher=[[ScienceBlogs|ScienceBlogs LLC]] |type=Blog |access-date=2014-01-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111226071454/http://scienceblogs.com/pharyngula/2007/01/jonathan_wells_knows_nothing_a.php |archive-date=December 26, 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://scienceblogs.com/aetiology/2007/01/wells_at_yale.php |title=Whereby Jon Wells is smacked down by an undergrad in the Yale Daily News |last=Smith |first=Tara C. |date=January 31, 2007 |website=Aetiology |publisher=ScienceBlogs LLC |type=Blog |access-date=2014-01-18 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120507180233/http://scienceblogs.com/aetiology/2007/01/wells_at_yale.php |archive-date=May 7, 2012 }}</ref> In 2011, Wells responded in  ''[[Science and Culture Today]]'':<blockquote>Since then, many of my critics have quoted the now-infamous line, "Father's words, my studies, and my prayers convinced me that I should devote my life to destroying Darwinism." (For a sampling, just do a Google search on the words.) Remarkably, Darwinists never quote much else from my essay, even though the 18 words in this one line represent only 1% of it, while a subsequent passage dealing with my scientific reasons for rejecting Darwinism represents 37%. Talk about quote mining...

Nor (as far as I know) have any Darwinists bothered to learn anything about the context in which I wrote the essay. If they had, they would know that Reverend Moon did not instruct or command me to destroy Darwinism (though years later he commended me on publishing Icons of Evolution.)

So, can I be trusted to say anything concerning the biological sciences? I freely admit that I was motivated to pursue a biology Ph.D., in part, because of my religious views. On the other hand, Francis Crick freely admitted (to historian Horace Freeland Judson) that he went into biology, in part, because of his atheistic views. What ultimately mattered in Crick's case was not his motivation, but whether his biological claims were consistent with the evidence. The same is true in my case.<ref name=":2" /></blockquote>He wrote articles for the Discovery Institute, ''[[WorldNetDaily]]'', ''[[Access Research Network|Origins & Design]]'', and other sympathetic publications attacking evolution and defending intelligent design.<ref name="discovery, search, wells">{{cite web |url=http://www.discovery.org/scripts/viewDB/index.php?command=submitSearchQuery&query=Jonathan%20Wells&orderBy=date&orderDir=DESC&searchBy=author&searchType=all |title=Article Database |website=Discovery Institute |location=Seattle, WA |access-date=2013-12-12 |archive-date=2011-07-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726010636/http://www.discovery.org/scripts/viewDB/index.php?command=submitSearchQuery&query=Jonathan%20Wells&orderBy=date&orderDir=DESC&searchBy=author&searchType=all |url-status=dead }} List of articles written by Jonathan Wells.</ref> In 1997, he presented a paper titled "Evolution by Design" at the Unification Church sponsored [[International Conference on the Unity of the Sciences]] in Washington, D.C.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tparents.org/library/unification/talks/wells/nat-select.htm |title=Evolution by Design |last=Wells |first=Jonathan |website=True Parents Organization |location=Denver, CO |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref>

In 1999, Wells debated with the New Mexicans for Science and Reason.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nmsr.org/jonwells.htm |title=The C-Files: Jonathan Wells |website=New Mexicans for Science and Reason |location=Peralta, NM |access-date=2008-05-17}}</ref> He was one of the contributors to ''[[Natural History (magazine)|Natural History]]'' magazine's 2002 debate between intelligent design advocates and evolution supporters.<ref>{{cite journal |editor-last1=Milner |editor-first1=Richard |editor1-link=Richard Milner (historian) |editor-last2=Maestro |editor-first2=Vittorio |date=April 2002 |title=Intelligent Design? |url=http://www.actionbioscience.org/evolution/nhmag.html |journal=[[Natural History (magazine)|Natural History]] |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref> In 2005, he debated [[Massimo Pigliucci]] on the [[PBS]] talk show ''[[Uncommon Knowledge]]''.<ref>{{cite episode |title=MONKEY BUSINESS: Evolution and Intelligent Design |url=http://www.hoover.org/multimedia/uncommon-knowledge/26902 |access-date=2008-07-17 |series=[[Uncommon Knowledge]] |first1=Peter (host) |last1=Robinson |author-link1=Peter Robinson (speechwriter) |first2=Pigliucci |last2=Massimo |author-link2=Massimo Pigliucci |first3=Jonathan |last3=Wells |network=[[PBS]] |station=[[KQEH|KTEH]] |date=January 14, 2005 |publisher=[[Hoover Institution]] |location=Stanford, CA |archive-date=2011-05-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110519194756/http://www.hoover.org/multimedia/uncommon-knowledge/26902 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Pigliucci said that Wells "clearly lied" during his debates and misrepresented his agenda and science, as well as not understanding some of the theories he tried to attack.<ref>[[#Pigliucci 2002|Pigliucci 2002]], pp. 44–45</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Pennock |first=Robert T. |author-link=Robert T. Pennock |date=September 2003 |title=Creationism and Intelligent Design |url=https://www.msu.edu/~pennock5/research/papers/Pennock_Creationism%2BID.pdf |journal=Annual Review of Genomics and Human Genetics |volume=4 |pages=143–163 |pmid=14527300 |doi=10.1146/annurev.genom.4.070802.110400 |access-date=2008-07-16}}</ref>

Wells was one of the signatories of the Discovery Institute's "[[A Scientific Dissent From Darwinism]]," a petition which the intelligent design movement uses to promote intelligent design by attempting to cast doubt on evolution.<ref name="Chang">{{cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=February 21, 2006 |title=Few Biologists but Many Evangelicals Sign Anti-Evolution Petition |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/02/21/science/sciencespecial2/21peti.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=2008-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.discovery.org/scripts/viewDB/filesDB-download.php?command=download&id=660 |title=A Scientific Dissent From Darwinism |website=Discovery Institute |location=Seattle, WA |format=PDF |access-date=2008-05-05}}</ref> He is also the author of "Ten questions to ask your biology teacher about evolution" for high school students, which is published by the Discovery Institute. The [[National Center for Science Education]] has issued a list of answers to the questions.<ref name="QuestionstoAsk">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/24/us/WEB-tenquestions.html |title=10 Questions, and Answers, About Evolution |newspaper=The New York Times |date=August 23, 2008 |access-date=2008-09-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://ncse.com/news/2008/08/teacher-front-line-002339 |title=A Teacher on the Front Line |date=August 24, 2008 |website=National Center for Science Education |location=Berkeley, CA |access-date=2008-09-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://ncse.com/creationism/analysis/10-answers-to-jonathan-wellss-10-questions |title=10 Answers to Jonathan Wells's '10 Questions' |date=October 17, 2008 |website=National Center for Science Education |location=Berkeley, CA |access-date=2008-02-19}}</ref>

===''Icons of Evolution''===
{{Main|Icons of Evolution}}
<!-- This use of this image does not have a corresponding rationale on the image's page. Please read [[Wikipedia:NFCC#10c]] [[File:Wells Icons of Evolution.jpg|thumb|left|''Icons of Evolution'']] -->
In 2000 Wells published his book ''[[Icons of Evolution]]'', in which he discusses 10 examples which he says show that many of the most commonly accepted arguments supporting [[evolution]] are invalid.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.discovery.org/a/3685 |title=Scientist Exposes Evolution's Weaknesses in Politically Incorrect Book About Darwinism and Intelligent Design |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=August 2, 2006 |website=Center for Science and Culture |publisher=Discovery Institute |location=Seattle, WA |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref>

According to [[Barbara Forrest]] and [[Paul R. Gross]], twelve reviews of Wells' book by subject matter experts from 2000 to 2004 came to the consensus that "Wells's icons are nothing more than the making—for politico-religious purposes—of an enormous mountain from a scattering of molehills".<ref name="CTH98">[[#Forrest & Gross 2004|Forrest & Gross 2004]], p. 98. Reviews specifically cited include those by David Ussery, [[Massimo Pigliucci]], [[Kevin Padian]] and Alan Gishlick.</ref> Scholars quoted in the work have accused Wells of purposely [[Fallacy of quoting out of context|misquoting them]] and misleading readers.<ref name="misquoting">[[#Forrest & Gross 2004|Forrest & Gross 2004]], p. 111. Quoting [[Bruce Grant (biologist)|Bruce Grant]]: "But should we blame Ms Rider for her outrage upon learning that moths were glued to trees? No. Instead I blame Dr Wells, who wrote the article she cites as her source of information. While he has done no work on industrial mechanism, he has written [an] opinion about that work. To one outside the field, he passes as a scholar, complete with Ph.D. Unfortunately, Dr Wells is intellectually dishonest. . . . He lavishly dresses his essays in quotations from experts (including some from me) which are generally taken out of context, and he systematically omits relevant details to make our conclusions seem ill founded, flawed, or fraudulent."</ref><ref name="Coyne-letter">{{cite news |last=Coyne |first=Jerry |date=December 6, 2000 |title=Criticism of moth study no challenge to evolution |url=http://www.jodkowski.pl/ka/PrattTribune005.html |newspaper=[[The Pratt Tribune]] |type=Letter to the editor |location=Pratt, KS |publisher=[[GateHouse Media]] |quote=Creationists such as Jonathan Wells claim that my criticism of [[Peppered moth evolution|these experiments]] casts strong doubt on Darwinism. But this characterization is false. ... My call for additional research on the moths has been wrongly characterized by creationists as revealing some fatal flaw in the theory of evolution. ... It is a classic creationist tactic (as exemplified in Wells' book, 'Icons of Evolution') to assert that healthy scientific debate is really a sign that evolutionists are either committing fraud or buttressing a crumbling theory. |access-date=2013-12-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116054931/http://www.jodkowski.pl/ka/PrattTribune005.html |archive-date=January 16, 2013 }}</ref> Biologist and skeptic [[Jerry Coyne]] wrote of ''Icons'', "Wells's book rests entirely on a flawed [[syllogism]]: ... textbooks illustrate evolution with examples; these examples are sometimes presented in incorrect or misleading ways; therefore evolution is a fiction."<ref name="Coyne" /><ref name="Talented">{{cite journal|last2=Gishlick|first2=Alan D.|date=March 2002|title=The Talented Mr. Wells|journal=[[The Quarterly Review of Biology]]|volume=77|issue=1|pages=33–37|doi=10.1086/339201|last1=Padian|first1=Kevin|author-link1=Kevin Padian}}<!--|access-date=2013-12-12--></ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Scott |first=Eugenie C. |author-link=Eugenie Scott |date=June 2001 |title=Fatally Flawed Iconoclasm |url=https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/science.1060716 |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |type=Book review |volume=292 |issue=5525 |pages=2257–2258 |doi=10.1126/science.1060716 |s2cid=153963713 |access-date=2007-05-17|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>[[#Pigliucci 2002|Pigliucci 2002]], pp. 252–264</ref><ref>[[#Forrest & Gross 2004|Forrest & Gross 2004]], p. 105</ref>

===Kansas evolution hearings===
{{Main|Kansas evolution hearings}}

In 2005, Wells participated in the [[Kansas evolution hearings]], which were [[boycott]]ed by mainstream scientists. There Wells testified:
 {{blockquote|I became convinced that the Darwinian theory is false because it conflicts with the evidence. ... I think the earth is probably four-and-a-half billion or so years old. But I'll tell you this, I used to-- I would have said, a few years ago, I'm convinced it's four-and-a-half billion years old. But the truth is I have not looked at the evidence. And I have become increasingly suspicious of the evidence that is presented to me and that's why at this point I would say probably it's four-and-a-half billion years old, but I haven't looked at the evidence. ... There are already scientists-- respected scientists in this country who do experiments on things that most people consider [[supernatural]], such as [[prayer]]. When [[Isaac Newton|Newton]] proposed the theory of [[gravitation]] it was dismissed as supernaturalism because it was action at a distance. What constitutes supernaturalism in today's science may very well not be supernatural in tomorrow's science.<ref name="TOKansas">{{cite web |url=http://www.talkorigins.org/faqs/kansas/kangaroo2.html#p681 |title=Kansas Evolution Hearings: Jonathan Wells, Bruce Simat, Giuseppe Sermonti, and Ralph Seelke |website=TalkOrigins Archive |publisher=The TalkOrigins Foundation, Inc. |location=Houston, TX |type=Transcript from the [[Kansas evolution hearings]] |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref>}}

Prior to the evolution hearings, in December 2000 after the [[Pratt County, Kansas]], school board revised its tenth-grade biology curriculum at the urging of intelligent design proponents to include material that encourages students to question the theory of evolution, ''[[The Pratt Tribune]]'' published a letter from  Jerry Coyne challenging Wells's characterization in an article of his work on [[peppered moths]], saying that his article appended to the ''Pratt'' standards was misused and being mischaracterized:
{{blockquote|Creationists such as Jonathan Wells claim that my criticism of these experiments casts strong doubt on Darwinism. But this characterization is false. ... My call for additional research on the moths has been wrongly characterized by creationists as revealing some fatal flaw in the theory of evolution. ... It is a classic creationist tactic (as exemplified in Wells' book, "Icons of Evolution") to assert that healthy scientific debate is really a sign that evolutionists are either committing fraud or buttressing a crumbling theory.<ref name="Coyne-letter" />}}

===''The Politically Incorrect Guide to Darwinism and Intelligent Design''===
In 2006, Wells published his second major book, ''The Politically Incorrect Guide to Darwinism and Intelligent Design'', which was part of a [[The Politically Incorrect Guide|series]] published by [[Regnery Publishing]]. The book was praised by [[Tom Bethell]], author of ''[[The Politically Incorrect Guide to Science]]'' (2005),<ref>{{cite news |last=Bethell |first=Tom |author-link=Tom Bethell |date=September 1, 2006 |title='Politically Incorrect' Series Takes on Darwinism and Intelligent Design |url=http://www.humanevents.com/2006/09/01/politically-incorrect-series-takes-on-darwinism-and-intelligent-design/ |work=[[Human Events]] |location=Washington, D.C. |publisher=Eagle Publishing, Inc. |issn=0018-7194 |access-date=2013-12-12 |archive-date=2013-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220073751/http://www.humanevents.com/2006/09/01/politically-incorrect-series-takes-on-darwinism-and-intelligent-design/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> but was described by Reed A. Cartwright of ''[[The Panda's Thumb (blog)|The Panda's Thumb]]'' weblog as being "not only politically incorrect but incorrect in most other ways as well: scientifically, logically, historically, legally, academically, and morally."<ref name="PoliticallyIncorrectReview">{{cite web |url=http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2006/08/the_politically.html |title=The Politically Incorrect Guide to Darwinism and Intelligent Design Review |date=August 19, 2006 |editor-last=Cartwright |editor-first=Reed A. |website=[[The Panda's Thumb (blog)|The Panda's Thumb]] |publisher=The TalkOrigins Foundation, Inc. |location=Houston, TX |type=Blog |access-date=2006-11-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060927161244/http://www.pandasthumb.org/archives/2006/08/the_politically.html |archive-date=September 27, 2006 }}</ref> Cartwright also edited a chapter-by-chapter critique of the book.<ref name="PoliticallyIncorrectReview"/> A quote from the book linking evolution to [[eugenics]], [[abortion]] and [[racism]] appeared on [[Starbucks]] paper cups in 2007.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rosen |first=Rebecca |date=May 16, 2009 |title=Starbucks stirs things up with controversial quotes |url=http://www.denverpost.com/ci_5902652?source=rss |newspaper=[[The Denver Post]] |publisher=[[MediaNews Group]] |access-date=2009-03-29}}</ref>

== HIV/AIDS denialism ==
{{Main|HIV/AIDS denialism}}

In 1991, Wells and his mentor Phillip E. Johnson signed an open letter which said in full:
{{blockquote|It is widely believed by the general public that a [[retrovirus]] called [[HIV]] causes the group [of] diseases called [[HIV/AIDS|AIDS]]. Many biochemical scientists now question this [[hypothesis]]. We propose that a thorough reappraisal of the existing evidence for and against this hypothesis be conducted by a suitable independent group. We further propose that critical [[Epidemiology|epidemiological]] studies be devised and undertaken.<ref name="AIDSgrouppeition">{{cite web |url=http://www.virusmyth.com/aids/group.htm |title=The Group |website=VirusMyth: A Rethinking AID$ Website |publisher=Robert Laarhoven |location=Hilversum, Netherlands |access-date=2013-12-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Quittman |first=Beth |date=September 8, 2006 |title=Undercover at the Discovery Institute |url=http://www.seattlest.com/archives/2006/09/08/undercover_at_the_discovery_institute.php |work=Seattlest |type=Blog |location=New York |publisher=[[Gothamist|Gothamist LLC]] |access-date=2008-07-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061020210815/http://www.seattlest.com/archives/2006/09/08/undercover_at_the_discovery_institute.php |archive-date=October 20, 2006 |url-status=dead }} Wells' "personal peculiarities include membership in the Moonies and support for AIDS reappraisal - the theory that the HIV is not the primary cause of AIDS."</ref><ref name="DenialismSun"/>}}

Wells and Johnson have been criticized, along with others, for their questioning of the scientific and medical consensus that HIV causes AIDS.<ref name="DenialismSun">{{cite news|title=Aids 'denialism' gathers strange bedfellows |url=http://www.canada.com/vancouversun/columnists/story.html?id=b0cb194b-51d3-4140-88f7-e4099445c554 |newspaper=[[The Vancouver Sun]] |location=Vancouver, BC |publisher=Postmedia Network Inc. |date=June 17, 2006 |access-date=2008-07-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140730105830/http://www.canada.com/vancouversun/columnists/story.html?id=b0cb194b-51d3-4140-88f7-e4099445c554 |archive-date=July 30, 2014 }}</ref>  In the ''[[Washington University Law Review]]'', Matthew J. Brauer, [[Barbara Forrest]], and [[Steven Gey|Steven G. Gey]] faulted Wells, Johnson, and others for denying the HIV/AIDS connection and promoting [[denialism]] via a petition which did not have any scientific support.<ref name="science_yet">{{cite journal |last1=Brauer |first1=Matthew J. |last2=Forrest |first2=Barbara |last3=Gey |first3=Steven G. |author-link3=Steven Gey |year=2005 |title=Is It Science Yet?: Intelligent Design Creationism and the Constitution |url=http://digitalcommons.law.wustl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1229&context=lawreview |format=PDF |journal=[[Washington University Law Review]] |volume=83 |issue=1 |pages=79–80 |issn=2166-7993 |access-date=2009-06-23 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220073757/http://digitalcommons.law.wustl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1229&context=lawreview |archive-date=2013-12-20 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Wells had two children—Josie and Peter—with his wife, Lucy.<ref name=":0" /> He died on September 19, 2024 (his 82nd birthday), at his home in [[Washington (state)|Washington]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Farewell to Jonathan Wells, Iconoclastic Scientist|first=David|last=Klinghoffer|date=September 24, 2024|website=[[Evolution News & Science Today]]|publication-place=Seattle|publisher=[[Discovery Institute]]|url=https://evolutionnews.org/2024/09/farewell-to-jonathan-wells-iconoclastic-scientist/}}</ref><ref name=":3" />
